patterns.comment: A title-line has an optional single ASCII separator and line value; accessibility line forms require a colon, and a description block reads through its first closing brace. architecture.md#composite-common-forms: The block form is accDescr, zero or more common whitespace characters, opening brace, any characters through the first closing brace.

Hidden YAML opens with three dashes, optional ASCII space/tab and LF; an unindented three-dash closer needs following common whitespace or EOF. The body-present alternative precedes the adjacent empty closer; this scope closes at the first qualifying closing line instead. architecture.md#hidden-forms-and-comments: A native comment has mark %%, then reads through the end of its line, excluding LF/CR but including U+2028 and U+2029.

A native hidden DIRECTIVE starts with optional ASCII space/tab and percent-pair plus opening brace, then reads through the first percent-pair closer satisfying the whitespace or EOF boundary. architecture.md#hidden-forms-and-comments: A native comment has mark %%, then reads through the end of its line, excluding LF/CR but including U+2028 and U+2029.

A native comment has mark %% and reads through the end of its line, excluding LF/CR but including U+2028 and U+2029. Earlier strings, labels, and common values own text they enclose. architecture.md#hidden-forms-and-comments: A native comment has mark %%, then reads through the end of its line, excluding LF/CR but including U+2028 and U+2029.

A label first tries a complete double-quoted string followed immediately by the closing bracket, then the same with single quotes. Choose the label alternative on the common converted diagram text: makes a complete HTML tag own its quoted attribute values before the lookahead tests the closing string quote. The string rule reads the authored quotes, escapes and directives. A common comment after a line separator or paragraph separator ends this value before the separator. The lookahead reads each content alternative whole; a backslash before an HTML tag remains ordinary text so that the tag owns its attribute quotes. architecture.md#icons-strings-and-bracketed-labels: An icon is an opening parenthesis, a nonempty name of ASCII letters, digits, underscores, dashes and colons, then a closing parenthesis. common.md#html-attribute-quotes: The attribute part may span lines, and it ends at the first `>`. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

String escape recognition applies to the complete quoted alternatives of a bracketed label. architecture.md#icons-strings-and-bracketed-labels: An icon is an opening parenthesis, a nonempty name of ASCII letters, digits, underscores, dashes and colons, then a closing parenthesis.

When neither complete quoted alternative matches, the bare label reads characters other than either bracket, CR or LF. Quotes and backslashes remain bare text, and the closing bracket leaves the following in keyword outside the label. A bare label treats quotes as ordinary characters, so no HTML rule can extend it beyond its closing bracket. patterns.comment: And: Keywords junction, service, column, group, align, row, and in have a longer-ID alternative; longer names such as serviceX and columnar are IDs. An ID cannot end with dash. architecture.md#ordered-rules: Word keywords have an explicit longer ID alternative; both dash rules have a longer hidden YAML alternative.

patterns.comment: The arrow has a colon before its first port direction and after its second; group-modifier is opening brace, group, and closing brace. architecture.md#grammar: An unlabelled edge uses contiguous double dash, while a labelled edge has a label between two single dashes.

architecture-string.comment: A string is single-quoted or double-quoted, closes with the same quote, and may be empty; backslash takes the next character other than LF, CR, LS or PS. architecture.md#icons-strings-and-bracketed-labels: An icon is an opening parenthesis, a nonempty name of ASCII letters, digits, underscores, dashes and colons, then a closing parenthesis.
